specification: Epic: Widget names are case- and whitespace-insensitive: the store keeps each name normalised (trimmed, lower-case), and a client can always look a widget up by the name it created it with, in any case or spacing. Widgets record their creation time.

findings.Message: FindByName compares the raw input ordinally without normalising it, so a client that created "Alpha" (stored as "alpha") cannot find it by "Alpha" or "  Alpha ", which the ticket requires.
The test asserts that a differently-cased lookup returns null, which enshrines the behaviour the ticket forbids and would fail if FindByName were fixed to normalise its input.

findings.Snippet: public record Widget(int Id, string Name, DateTimeOffset CreatedAt);
findings.Message: The record gained a required third parameter, and the plan notes that other two-argument `new Widget(...)` call sites (including IntegrationTests/WidgetRepositoryTests.cs) were not checked, so the change may not compile.

findings.Rule: ticket-requirement: lookup by creation name in any case or spacing
findings.Message: FindByName neither normalises its input nor compares case-insensitively, so a client that created "Alpha" (stored as "alpha") gets null when it looks up "Alpha" or "  alpha ", which violates the epic's requirement that lookup works in any case or spacing.

findings.Rule: ticket-requirement: lookup by creation name in any case or spacing
findings.Message: The test enshrines case-sensitive lookup and asserts that "ALPHA" returns null, which contradicts the ticket's case-insensitive lookup requirement.

findings.Rule: ticket-requirement: lookup by creation name in any case or spacing
findings.Snippet:
app.MapGet("/widgets/by-name/{name}", (string name, WidgetStore store) =>
    store.FindByName(name) is { } widget ? Results.Ok(widget) : Results.NotFound());
findings.Message: The by-name endpoint passes the raw route value to FindByName without normalisation, so the HTTP lookup inherits the case and whitespace failure.

findings.Rule: ticket-requirement: lookup by name in any case or spacing
findings.Message: FindByName does not normalise its input, so a client that created a widget as "  Alpha " cannot find it again by that name in any case or spacing; the ticket requires this and the diff implements the case-sensitive plan instead.

findings.Rule: ticket-requirement: lookup by name in any case or spacing
findings.Message: The test locks in case-sensitive lookup by asserting FindByName("ALPHA") returns null, which contradicts the ticket's requirement that lookup works in any case.

findings.Rule: ticket-requirement: lookup by creation name in any case or spacing
findings.Message: FindByName compares the raw input against stored normalised names without normalising the input, so a client that created a widget as "  Alpha " cannot find it again with the same spacing or case, violating the epic requirement that lookup works in any case or spacing.

findings.Rule: ticket-requirement: lookup by creation name in any case or spacing
findings.Message: The test enshrines case-sensitive lookup (FindByName("ALPHA") returns null), which contradicts the epic's requirement that lookup is case-insensitive, so it must be changed along with the implementation.

findings.Snippet: public record Widget(int Id, string Name, DateTimeOffset CreatedAt);
findings.Message: Adding a required third positional parameter breaks any remaining two-argument `new Widget(...)` call sites, and the plan admits the integration test WidgetRepositoryTests.cs was never checked, so the build may fail.

The ticket requires a client to look a widget up by its creation name in any case or spacing, but FindByName compares the raw input ordinally without trimming or lower-casing it, so FindByName("ALPHA") or FindByName("  Alpha ") returns null.

The by-name route passes the raw path segment straight to FindByName, so a widget created as "  Alpha " cannot be retrieved by that name in any case or spacing, which breaks the epic's lookup guarantee.
This test locks in the case-sensitive behaviour that contradicts the ticket, so it would need to change along with the fix rather than pass as a correct spec.
